title: A Conditional No-Hair Theorem for Transformers: How Language Models Forget Their Prompt
abstract: arXiv:2610.24133v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A black hole retains only a few conserved charges of the matter it formed from. We are inspired to make the analogy and we ask how much an autoregressive transformer retains of its prompt after generating $t$ tokens. For two prompts followed by the same continuation, the difference of their hidden states decays approximately as a power law $t^{-\alpha}$, where $\alpha=1$ is the rate at which a fixed prompt's share of uniform attention shrinks. Beyond the first layers, trained models forget faster ($\alpha\approx0.55$--$0.7$) than untrained ones of the same architecture ($\alpha\approx0.2$--$0.5$). For finite-depth pre-LN softmax transformers with bounded attention logits and non-degenerate pre-norm activations, we prove that this offset is $O\big(P(\log t)^{L-1}/t\big)$ for prompt length $P$ and depth $L$: the prompt's direct influence is diluted as the context grows, and \emph{relay} through continuation tokens adds only logarithmic

translated_title: 变换器的条件无毛定理：语言模型如何遗忘其提示词
translated_abstract: 黑洞只保留其形成物质的少数几个守恒荷。受此类比启发，我们提出这样一个问题：自回归变换器在生成 $t$ 个 token 之后，对其提示词还能保留多少信息。对于两个后续生成相同续写的提示词，它们隐状态之间的差异近似按幂律 $t^{-\alpha}$ 衰减，其中 $\alpha=1$ 是固定提示词在均匀注意力中所占份额收缩的速率。在最初几层之外，经过训练的模型遗忘得更快（$\alpha\approx0.55$–$0.7$），而相同架构下未训练的模型遗忘较慢（$\alpha\approx0.2$–$0.5$）。对于注意力对数几率有界、前置层归一化激活非退化的有限深度 pre-LN softmax 变换器，我们证明了这一偏移量为 $O\big(P(\log t)^{L-1}/t\big)$，其中 $P$ 为提示词长度、$L$ 为网络深度：提示词的直接影响随着上下文的增长而被稀释，而通过续写 token 进行的“接力”传播仅带来对数级……
tldr: 本文受黑洞无毛定理启发，通过实验和理论证明自回归 Transformer 对提示词的记忆在生成过程中以幂律衰减（训练后模型 α≈0.55–0.7，快于未训练模型的 α≈0.2–0.5），并证明了提示词影响按 $O(P(\log t)^{L-1}/t)$ 速率被稀释的条件无毛定理。
en_tdlr: Inspired by the black hole no-hair theorem, this paper empirically and theoretically shows that a transformer's memory of its prompt decays as a power law (trained models forget faster with α≈0.55–0.7 than untrained ones), proving a conditional no-hair theorem that prompt influence is diluted as O(P(log t)^{L-1}/t) as the context grows.
